mode: Independent read-only analytic/source review; no new model or suite run

assumptions: H is self-adjoint, H>=0, H Omega=0 in the full given CAR representation.
alpha_t(A)=exp(+itH) A exp(-itH) is the chosen mathematical Heisenberg convention.
A is bounded and lies in F(I). There exist epsilon>0 and a proper larger interval J with alpha_t(A) in F(J) for every |t|<epsilon. Geometric rotation covariance is sufficient.
Omega is separating for F(J), hence for F(I). Proper intervals are nonempty, open, connected and nondense, with I and its small translates contained in J.
A Omega is in an exact energy eigenspace E>0 of this same H. Zero vector is allowed and already implies A0 by separation.
proof_steps: For |t|<epsilon, B_t=alpha_t(A)-exp(itE)A belongs to F(J) and B_t Omega=0. Separation gives B_t=0.
For any real t choose integer N with |t/N|<epsilon. The automorphism group law extends alpha_t(A)=exp(itE)A to all t.

Taking adjoints and applying to Omega gives exp(itH)A*Omega=exp(-itE)A*Omega. By the spectral theorem A*Omega has energy -E, so positivity forces it to vanish. No differentiation of unbounded H or domain assumption on A*Omega is needed.
A* belongs to F(I); separation gives A*=0 and A=0.
lemma.sign_check: With source U(t)=exp(-itH) and conjugation U A U*, replace exp(itE) by exp(-itE) consistently. The negative-energy conclusion for the adjoint is unchanged.
lemma.separation_not_separability: The needed property is that Omega is a separating vector for the local algebra. Separable Hilbert space alone is irrelevant.

instrument_corollary_review.review_type: Independent agent analytic review of the direct corollary; no new numerical or formal proof run
assumptions: All full-net, positive-energy, same-vacuum, bounded-local-operator and local time-covariance/separation hypotheses of the preceding lemma hold.
An outcome has finitely or countably many bounded Kraus operators A_j in the same proper interval algebra F(I).

sigma=T(|Omega><Omega|)=sum_j |A_j Omega><A_j Omega| is a positive normal output. For a physical outcome this is trace class with finite probability; for example sum_j A_j* A_j<=I ensures trace-nonincreasing normal convergence.
The output support is contained in the exact spectral subspace H_E=Ran(1_{E}(H)) for E>0, here E32. Support in the actual finite R_b4 packet is sufficient because that packet is contained in H32.
proof: Set v_j=A_j Omega, P=1_{E}(H), Q=I-P. The support assumption gives Q sigma Q=0.
For a trace-class outcome, normality/monotone convergence of the positive partial sums gives Tr(Q sigma)=sum_j ||Q v_j||^2=0. Every summand is nonnegative, hence Q v_j=0 for every j.

Equivalently, even without using a trace, for every xi in Ran Q, normal vector functionals give 0=<xi,sigma xi>=sum_j |<xi,v_j>|^2. Positivity forces every v_j orthogonal to Ran Q. This avoids an unjustified exchange of a nonnormal limit and trace.
Thus each A_j Omega lies in the exact E>0 eigenspace. The proved local eigenpacket lemma yields A_j=0 individually, including the zero-vector case by separation.
Consequently sigma=0 and its success probability is0. Renormalization cannot produce a pure or mixed exact E32 state with nonzero outcome probability.
instrument_corollary_review.packet_metric_precision: If a projector onto the five-state R_b4 packet is used, it means the orthogonal projector in the actual full CAR Hilbert-space metric, not a raw coordinate cut assuming Gram I. Only the inclusion Ran(P_packet) subset H32 is needed.
instrument_corollary_review.projection_in_the_proof_is_not_a_prepara: The global spectral projector P_E and Q are mathematical support tests. No claim that they themselves belong to the local algebra or are physically available filters is made.
instrument_corollary_review.normal_convergence_precision: A normal trace-nonincreasing Kraus outcome has trace-norm convergence of its positive vacuum-output partial sums, sufficient for the displayed norm-square identity. Bare unspecified convergence is not substituted for normality. The vector-functional proof also establishes the conclusion for positive ultraweak limits where a finite trace was not assumed.

luders_case.statement: Applies to a proper-local original Lüders projection P in F(I), with one Kraus operator A=P, or to a finite/countable same-local Kraus outcome of the stated type.
luders_case.independent_consistency_check: For any orthogonal projection P, <Omega,P Omega>=||P Omega||^2. If P Omega lies entirely at strictly positive energy, it is orthogonal to Omega, so P Omega=0. Local separation then gives P0. This elementary special case agrees with the general Kraus result.

scope_limits: The conclusion allows pure or mixed outputs and finitely/countably many local Kraus terms; positivity prevents cancellations outside the target spectral subspace.
It is not a theorem about every abstract normal AQFT CP map: an arbitrary CP map is not assumed to possess bounded Kraus operators inside this same local algebra.
No conclusion is drawn about approximate target preparation, quantitative success/energy/norm tradeoffs, different initial states, altered Hamiltonians or enlarged/global preparation procedures.
No extension to unbounded field insertions, uncontrolled infinite histories or a physically derived P1 preparation menu is asserted.
The result uses the full H_alpha=8K_alpha, not only the compressed quartic matrix. Exact H32 support is essential.
